name: IEC even-parity element
summary: Element marked 2k whose output is active when an even number of its inputs are active.
description: The 2k qualifier means the output is active when an even number of inputs, including none, are active. It is the multi-input generalisation of exclusive-NOR and is used in parity generation and checking for data words.

On communication or memory logic drawings the even-parity element may feed a parity bit or compare a received parity bit. The drawing should indicate how many inputs are grouped, often with an input-line grouping or a bus notation, because the function depends on the full set.
The element gives no information about word framing or when the parity result is sampled. Clocking and latching are separate elements.
readingNotes: Count all inputs, including any shown by bus notation.
Zero active inputs counts as even.
drawingChecklist: Use 2k rather than =1 or = for parity.
Show where the result is latched or compared.
distinction: The 2k+1 element is its complement and gives odd parity.
